name: NTPD — New Tokyo Police Department
desc: New Tokyo's overstretched law enforcement. Underfunded, outgunned, but they keep the streets from total collapse. They value reliability over flash.
flavor: The badge doesn't mean much anymore. But the people who wear it still do.

10.name: Acquaintance
10.desc: You've been flagged in the system. Not a threat — yet.

25.name: Trusted
25.desc: You've done favors. They look the other way when you pass.

50.name: Allied
50.desc: An unofficial asset. They call you before they call backup.

75.name: Honored
75.desc: The Commissioner knows your name. That means something.

100.name: Legend
100.desc: You ARE the law. At least, the part that works.

notes: The 'safe' faction. Moderate gear, good blueprints for defense. Buying Exile gear costs NTPD rep — forces a choice. Aegis-Tac is their equipment supplier. Shibata Arms weapons available through their vendor (police use ballistics).
fatherContext: Kazuo Hayashi was a decorated NTPD officer specializing in mecha-related crime. He was charged with corruption — accepting bribes to ignore illegal weapons shipments. The department is divided: some officers believe the charges, others think he was framed. His case file is sealed by Internal Affairs.
playerImpact: The Hayashi name opens doors with sympathetic officers and closes them with administrators who want the case buried. At Allied rep, an officer quietly provides Kazuo's sealed case file — the first concrete evidence the charges were fabricated.

name: Kuroda Military Command
desc: Kuroda Heavy Industries' private military arm. They protect corporate assets, run the restricted zones, and possess the heaviest firepower in New Tokyo. They respect strength, not words.
flavor: They don't ask twice. They don't need to.

0.name: Hostile
0.desc: You are a trespasser. Engage on sight.

10.name: Tolerated
10.desc: You've proven useful. They won't shoot first.

50.name: Operative
50.desc: You have a handler. You have clearance. You have a leash.

75.name: Commander
75.desc: Field command authority. Steele considers you an equal.

100.name: Legend
100.desc: Kuroda's ghost. The soldier who doesn't exist.

notes: The 'heavy' faction. Best armor, best weapons, highest stat requirements. Anti-Exile (completing Exile missions costs military rep). Defeating Steele gives +15 rep in one shot — earning respect through combat, not politics. Type 90 custom blueprint at 75 is the endgame Heavy frame goal.
fatherContext: Kazuo's investigation touched Kuroda's weapons contracts. Commander Steele specifically remembers him — his report crossed her desk before it was classified. Whether Kuroda actively participated in his downfall or was used as a shield is ambiguous.
playerImpact: Steele recognizes the player during combat ('Was his name—'). At high rep, she privately shares: 'Your father's report was legitimate. I verified it. Then it disappeared from the system.'

name: The Underground
desc: The black market network under the Neon Bazaar. Scrapyard mechanics, smugglers, fixers, and everyone who fell through New Tokyo's cracks. They trade in favors and stolen goods.
flavor: Down here, everyone's got a past. Nobody asks about it.

0.name: Outsider
0.desc: They see you but don't talk to you.

10.name: Regular
10.desc: They nod when you walk in. That's currency here.

25.name: Connected
25.desc: You know people who know people. Doors open.

50.name: Fixer
50.desc: You're the one people call when things need to get done quietly.

75.name: Kingmaker
75.desc: You don't just live in the Underground. You shape it.

100.name: Legend
100.desc: The Underground IS you. Every deal, every favor, every secret — it all connects back.

notes: The 'starter' faction — first contact, cheapest gear, widest variety. Three manufacturers (Red Creek, Sora, KZ) give breadth. The Hayabusa Restoration blueprint at 75 is the mid-endgame goal for the narrative-focused player. Anti-NTPD on specific actions but not by default — you CAN be friends with both.
fatherContext: Ichiro Hayashi has been part of Underground trading networks for decades. Kazuo used the scrapyard to modify mechas off the books — some for police use, some for Underground contacts. He was respected for his engineering, not his badge.
playerImpact: The player is treated as family. Older fixers remember 'Ichiro's kid' and extend goodwill. Iron Volk targeted the scrapyard because word on the street says something important is hidden there.

name: Taeyang Syndicate
desc: Taeyang Forge's shadow operations in New Tokyo. Thermal weapons, illegal shipments, and a reputation for burning anyone who crosses them. Their loyalty is bought with fire.
flavor: They don't shake hands. Too hot.

0.name: Unknown
0.desc: Taeyang doesn't know you. That's healthy.

10.name: Customer
10.desc: You buy their weapons. They tolerate your existence.

25.name: Associate
25.desc: You've done a job for them. They send work your way.

50.name: Enforcer
50.desc: You carry their weapons. You carry their reputation.

75.name: Inner Circle
75.desc: You know where the real shipments go. You know the real prices.

100.name: Legend
100.desc: The flame that doesn't go out. Taeyang's will made metal.

repSources.source: Use Taeyang weapons in arena victories

notes: The 'fire' faction. Thermal specialization — all blueprints revolve around heat management and thermal damage. Defeating Crimson Nail gives +12 rep (Taeyang respects those who defeat their best). The Supernova Custom blueprint at 75 is the endgame energy weapon.
fatherContext: Kazuo was investigating Taeyang's illegal thermal weapons shipments. When the investigation threatened to expose the protection network, Taeyang's corporate arm activated the response: fabricated charges, sealed files, a convenient disappearance.
playerImpact: Taeyang leadership knows the Hayashi name. The player's growing reputation makes them nervous. At high rep, an insider leaks a partial document: the original order to 'resolve the Hayashi situation.'

name: Phantom Collective
desc: What remains of Phantom Works after the corporate crackdown. Scattered, hidden, brilliant. They build technology that shouldn't exist and fight a war no one else knows about. They knew Dad.
flavor: They don't exist. That's their greatest weapon.

0.name: Unaware
0.desc: You don't even know they exist.

10.name: Contact
10.desc: Someone reached out. A dead drop. An encrypted message.

25.name: Asset
25.desc: They trust you with small things. Deliveries. Messages. Surveillance.

50.name: Operative
50.desc: You're part of something bigger. Dad's network. His legacy.

75.name: Inner Cell
75.desc: You know the plan. You know what Dad was building. You know why.

100.name: Legend
100.desc: You finished what he started. The Phantom Collective's purpose is fulfilled.

notes: The 'story' faction. Everything ties to Dad. Highest rep penalties for betrayal (-15 to -20). Daewon Dynamics is their 'legit' front. Phantom Works is the real tech. Hayabusa Mk.II blueprint at 75 is THE narrative reward — Dad's unfinished frame. Defeating Null gives +20 rep in one shot. Anti-Kuroda and anti-NTPD on betrayal, but neutral by default.
fatherContext: Kazuo came to Phantom because he had nowhere else to go. They shared intelligence, resources, and a vision. The Hayabusa Mk.II was their joint project — Kazuo's engineering combined with Phantom's bleeding-edge technology.
playerImpact: Null tests the player out of necessity — Kazuo's child must be strong enough. The Phantom Collective has been waiting for someone to continue Kazuo's work. They are patient, but desperate.
